reply:
Coalescing happens when an op is added to the outbox, and only between ops with the same `target_id` (`docs/DESIGN.md:1857`). The doc says it's needed for correctness, not just speed: without it, an edit or delete can reach the server for a message the server has never seen.

```openui-lang

header = CardHeader("Outbox coalescing rules", "DESIGN.md §10.4")

colQueued = Col("Queued", ["send", "send", "send", "edit", "edit", "react(add)", "read(ord=5)"])
colNew = Col("New op", ["edit", "delete", "react", "edit", "delete", "react(remove)", "read(ord=9)"])
colResult = Col("Result", ["Put the new body into the send's payload; one op remains", "Drop both; nothing is sent to the server", "Keep both, in order; the react must follow the send", "Keep the last edit", "Drop the edit, keep the delete", "Drop both (same emoji and user)", "Keep the higher ord (max-register)"])
note = Callout("warning", "Add this early", "The doc warns that adding coalescing later means checking every op type against every other op type.")
ref = FileRef("docs/DESIGN.md", 1848, "§10.4 Outbox coalescing")
```

These seven pairs are the only ones the table lists. It doesn't cover `blob_upload`, `join` or `leave`, or pairs like `edit` then `react`. The doc does say elsewhere that a `blob_upload` must finish before the `send` that uses it (line 1845).
